tasks.short: Verify analytical systems with an independent model and sign the break.

steps.what: State what the independent model must verify in the analytical systems.
Apply a second formula to the analytical systems' inputs.
Tie both results to the same source rows.
Investigate a break between the independent models.
Sign the verification of the analytical systems.

tasks.design: The analyst states what the independent check must prove, and a second formula runs on the same inputs. Both results are tied to the source rows. Investigating a break, and signing the verification, stay with the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: The second result was rebuilt by hand, so a break could not be compared on the same rows.
tasks.enabler_now: A second formula and a tie-out are rules once the aim and the inputs exist. Stating the aim, and explaining a break, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A break where the two models answer different questions.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when the systems are wrong and when the check was aimed at the wrong thing.
tasks.altitude: The second result is ready before the investigation. The analyst still states the aim and can refuse to sign. Decision rights on the verification do not move.

reach.role: Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents
reach.task: Say which tied totals an examination will recompute
reach.learn: Which source rows a later examination expects to see

evidence.claim: A tool pulls source evidence and runs a test of details, and the team reviews and signs off.
In a published spreadsheet-agent test, most models ended a cash waterfall at €1.16 million, not €580,000.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from a check question to a signed verification. Fixing the system is a later task.

Structured fields are aim, input id, system result, second result and source row. The analyst writes the aim; the system produces its result. Fallback: a pair that does not share a source row is not treated as a tie.
Configure the second formula on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new input added to the second formula.
unknowns: Whether the analytical systems expose the inputs the second formula needs.
Whether a signed verification blocks use of the system.
research_questions: What share of checks share source rows between the two results?
How often is the aim rewritten after a break?

incremental.description: Add an input to the second formula

approvals.approved_version: verification the analyst signed against the tied pair

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the systems do not share source rows, so the tie is manual and the investigation is unchanged. High: rows match and only the second formula shrinks. The aim and the break stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test analytical software against the requirements and accept or return it.

steps.what: Read the requirements and specifications for the analytical software.

loop.output: Statements that a test can pass or fail
loop.check: The analyst marks a statement that is too vague to test
loop.stop: One pass; a vague statement stays open
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements mix tables and prose, so a fixed list misses sentences

steps.what: Build the analytical software against the requirements.
Run acceptance tests named in the requirements.
Meet when testing shows the software missed the requirements.
Accept the analytical software or send it back.

tasks.design: Requirements are turned into statements a test can fail. The developer builds the analytical software. The analyst runs the named tests, meets on a failure, and accepts the software or sends it back.
tasks.previous_blocker: Acceptance was a meeting with no list of statements, so a failure had no expected result.
tasks.enabler_now: Named tests can be run once statements exist. Judging a failure the test does not explain, and accepting the software, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A requirement too vague to become a test.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when a passed test still misses the scope.
tasks.altitude: Tests are ready before the meeting. The analyst still attends the failure discussion and can send the software back. Decision rights on acceptance do not move.

reach.task: Say which operational counts the software must reproduce
reach.learn: Which user requirements come from an operational neighbour

evidence.claim: Accepting software against user requirements stays with the person who will rely on it.
Running a named test with an expected result is a rules task.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. The developer's build is not the analyst's saving. Boundary: from requirements to an acceptance decision. Writing the software is the developer's task.

Structured fields are requirement id, expected result and test status. The user requirements produce the statement; the build produces the actual result. Fallback: a requirement with no expected result is not a pass.
Configure the test run on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new requirement added to the test list.
unknowns: Whether requirements already state an expected result.
Whether the developer and the analyst are different people.
research_questions: What share of requirements can be turned into a test?
How often is software sent back after the tests pass?

incremental.description: Add a requirement to the acceptance tests

approvals.approved_version: acceptance decision the analyst made against the test log

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: requirements are vague, so tests are written during the meeting and acceptance is unchanged. High: statements exist and only the test run shrinks. The meeting and the decision stay. Developer time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer on trading strategies and note the technique the room wants.

steps.what: Prepare a one-page pack on trading strategies and market conditions.

loop.input: Recent trading performance and the questions for the conference
loop.output: One page with strategy, figure and source
loop.check: The analyst removes a figure that is not in the performance extract
loop.stop: One pass; a question with no figure stays as a question
loop.why_not_simpler: The questions are prose, so a fixed performance report is not the pack

steps.what: Confer with other analysts on trading strategies and market conditions.
Note the quantitative techniques the conference wants developed.

tasks.design: A one-page pack is prepared from performance figures before the conference. The conference itself stays a meeting. The analyst notes which quantitative techniques the room actually asked to develop.
tasks.previous_blocker: The pack was assembled in the meeting, so the hour was spent finding figures.
tasks.enabler_now: A short pack can be drafted from figures that already exist. The conference, and choosing which request is real, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A strategy discussion that the recent figures do not capture.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which comment is a request and which is only a view.
tasks.altitude: The pack is ready before the hour. The conference stays. The analyst can decline to write down a technique nobody asked for. Decision rights do not move.

reach.task: Say which market moves change an underwriting view
reach.learn: Which market moves an underwriting neighbour treats as material

evidence.claim: A conference about trading strategies stays with the people in the room.
A one-page pack limited to existing figures is a drafting task.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Colleagues' time in the same meeting is not removed from this task, because the analyst's presence is the work. Boundary: from a conference need to a technique request. Building the technique is later.
Structured fields are strategy, figure, source and request. Performance extracts produce the figure. Fallback: a figure not in the extract is removed from the pack.
Configure the performance extract on {BI} before custom code.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new figure on the pack.
unknowns: Whether performance figures are already extracted by strategy.
Whether the conference has a standing agenda.
research_questions: What share of the pack is figures already extracted?
How often is a spoken idea not written down as a request?

incremental.description: Add a figure to the conference pack

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: there is no extract, so the pack is made in the meeting and the conference is unchanged. High: figures exist and only the pack shrinks. The conference stays.

tasks.short: Consult traders and determine whether an improved application is needed.

steps.what: Consult traders on the need for improved analytical applications.
Group complaints into themes for improved analytical applications.

loop.output: Themes with a count and an example quote
loop.check: The analyst corrects a theme that merges two different needs
loop.stop: One pass; a note that fits no theme stays ungrouped
loop.why_not_simpler: Complaints are free text, so a fixed category list merges different needs

steps.what: Determine whether an improved analytical application is needed.
Confirm the need for the improved application before a build.

tasks.design: The analyst consults traders about gaps in current applications. Complaint notes are grouped into themes. Determining the need stays with the analyst, and a build is confirmed only from that need statement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were a pile of messages, so two complaints about different gaps looked like one request.
tasks.enabler_now: Free-text complaints can be grouped once notes exist. The interview, and deciding that a gap is a real need, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A complaint that is a one-off market, not a missing application.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which theme is worth a build.
tasks.altitude: Themes are ready after the interviews. The analyst still consults traders and can refuse a build. Decision rights on the need do not move.

reach.task: Say which application gaps show up in a claim review
reach.learn: Which trader complaints match a neighbouring team's gap

evidence.claim: Deciding that traders need a new application stays with the analyst who heard them.
Grouping free-text complaints is a classification task with a person correcting merged themes.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from trader conversations to a confirmed need. Building the application is later.
Structured fields are theme, count, example and decision. The interview produces the note. Fallback: a note that fits no theme is left ungrouped and is not counted as demand.
Configure the theme list in {DOCS} before custom code.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new theme the interviews start using.
unknowns: Whether trader complaints are already written down.
Whether a confirmed need is enough to start a build.
research_questions: What share of complaints fit an existing theme?
How often is a popular theme judged not to be a need?

incremental.description: Add a theme when interviews use a new gap

approvals.approved_version: need statement the analyst confirmed for this round of trader interviews

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complaints are not written down, so grouping happens in the interview and the judgement is unchanged. High: notes exist and only the grouping shrinks. The consultation and the need stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still stating what a check must prove, sitting in conferences and hearing traders. Second results and test logs are ready beforehand. The analyst can refuse a verification, a software acceptance or a build.
reach: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents: say which tied totals an examination will recompute
Insurance underwriters: say which market moves change an underwriting view
Claims adjusters, examiners, and investigators: say which application gaps show up in a claim review
skills_to_grow: Stating a verification aim that two results can actually share
Sending software back when a passed test still misses the scope
Leaving a trader complaint ungrouped when it is not demand
role.ambitious_version: Every signed verification shares source rows, every software acceptance cites a test, and a build starts only from a need the analyst has confirmed.
